description: Same direction/magnitude reassignment test as patch_reassignment_v1.json, run against the checkpoint-eval reproduction path (scripts/checkpoint_eval/dynapatch.py + scripts/deploy_from_checkpoints.sh) instead of a from-scratch training run.
rq: Mechanism: does input-specific matching, especially direction matching, explain held-out repair? -- sanity-checked against checkpoints rather than a fresh training run.
hypothesis: DynaPatch works partly because different inputs receive different correction directions matched to their error modes.
falsifier: The median RR_held advantage of the original assignment over global reassignment is at most 0.02, or fewer than 24 of 36 cells exceed the null 97.5th percentile.
support_rule: Support if the median advantage is greater than 0.05 and at least 30 of 36 cells exceed the null 97.5th percentile.

data.population: Rows where the frozen base prediction is wrong. Seed 101 only -- checkpoint-eval baselines/DynaPatch repair checkpoints only exist at seed 101 for the 6 baselines; DynaPatch's own repair checkpoints exist for all 3 seeds (see artifacts/checkpoints/MANIFEST.md), but this config stays at seed 101 to match what the baseline comparison in outputs/checkpoint_eval/ covers.

compute.device: CPU analysis from saved logits; invocation pins CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0

stopping_rule: Sanity check only -- compare against patch_reassignment_v1's from-scratch numbers, do not treat as a replacement for it.
